Situation Report — Day 27

  • Ceasefire / Talks: US announced a SECOND 10-day pause on energy strikes (deadline Apr 6, 2026 8 PM ET). Trump says Iran requested the pause and talks are "going very well." Iran denies direct talks. Pakistan mediating.
  • Air operations: NATO chief (TASS) says US flew ~5,000 sorties from European bases in the operation against Iran. Large sortie rate shows sustained long-range strike and ISR capacity.
  • Airspace & civil aviation: Flight-scan: 329 aircraft visible, 0 military. Airports closed: Iran, Israel, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan. Civilian travel and relief routes remain heavily restricted.
  • Accountability / War-crimes scrutiny: AP reports a US missile killed Iranian schoolchildren four months ago. Investigation and media focus continue. Political fallout may constrain US messaging.
  • Regional posture: Northern front (Hezbollah) continues daily activity (ongoing). Iran continues selective Hormuz passage for friendly states (Russia, India, China) — strategic alignments persist.
  • Note on reliability: Past pause (Mar 23, 5 days) was violated within hours by strikes on Isfahan and Khorramshahr. Pause credibility is conditional.
  • 🟢 Good News: A formal US pause announced and Pakistan mediation active.
  • Threat assessment: escalating

  • 🟢 חדשות טובות: הוכרזה הפוגה רשמית ופקיסטן מתווכת.
  • הערכת איום: escalating

Situation Report — Day 27 (last 2 hours)

  • No new public siren/strike alerts reported in this window.

Ceasefire / Diplomacy

  • US: President Trump announced a SECOND pause on energy-targeted strikes for 10 days (deadline Apr 6, 2026 8 PM ET), citing an "Iranian request" and progress in talks.
  • Iran denies direct talks. Pakistan is mediating.
  • AP/Pakistan reports say US and Iran have agreed wording of a deal — provisional step, not signed.
  • Context: first 5-day pause (Mar 23) was broken by US/Israeli strikes hours later.

Air Campaign & Airspace

  • Flight scans: regional airspace disruption continues. Current snapshots show 329 aircraft and earlier 568; 2 military flights identified (RCH462, RCH436).
  • Airports closed across the region: Iran, Israel, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Jordan — major travel/logistics halt.
  • TASS/NATO chief: US flew ~5,000 sorties from European bases during the operation — indicates sustained long-range effort.

Northern Border & Ground Threats

  • Hezbollah attacks continue daily on northern border (ongoing low-high intensity exchanges per routine reporting).

Cyber & Information

  • INCD reports cyber incidents in Israel have tripled year-on-year — increased targeting of infrastructure and military networks.

Media / Investigations

  • AP revisits an incident where a US missile killed Iranian schoolchildren months ago — potential political/legal fallout if confirmed.

International Posture

  • Iran allows Hormuz passage for select states (Russia, India, China) while restricting others — creates diplomatic split and shipping disruption.
  • 🟢 Good News: Pakistan mediation reports progress; US and Iran reportedly agreed wording — opens a limited de-escalation path.

Bottom line

  • Threat assessment: escalating
